newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait considers Rotterdam refinery expansion.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait considers Rotterdam refinery expansion.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) is considering plans to expand its Rotterdam refinery after the planned closure of its Stigsnaes refinery in Denmark, a KPC official was quoted on Sunday as saying.
KPC's managing director for marketing, Hani Hussein, "revealed that the Netherlands refinery might be expanded...after the closure of the Denmark refinery," al-Watan newspaper reported.

KPC said in December said it was considering boosting its Rotterdam refinery production capacity to 150,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 80,000, while the uncompetitive 59,000 bpd Stigsnaes refinery in Denmark would be closed in 1997.
KPC was studying proposals to sell storage facilities at the Stigsnaes refinery, the daily said. It planned to lay off 200 workers at the refinery, it said.
Kuwait, which has an OPEC oil production quota of two million bpd, has a refining capacity of about 250,000 bpd in Europe in addition to 895,000 bpd at home.

Al-Qabas newspaper on Sunday reported that KPC had launched a plan to restructure its loss-making, London-based subsidiary Kuwait Peteroleum International Ltd (KPI) to tackle what it called "stumbling activities".
KPI is in charge of Kuwait's refining operations and downstream marketing in Europe and Asia.
